conditions.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator omitted the bypass-opening step and thereby caused the start-up damage. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

evidence_items.text: Post-event inspection found an internal obstruction in the bypass path despite the bypass-valve handle being in the indicated open position.
A time-stamped witness record documents the operator moving the bypass-valve handle to the indicated open position before start-up.

V-001 sustained internal damage after start-up. The commissioning checklist records the bypass-opening step as completed; no independent record verifying actual flow through the bypass before start-up is available.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Mechanical obstruction inside the bypass valve or line restricting required start-up flow despite open handle indication.

evidence_against.relevance: Lack of real-time flow telemetry leaves precise moment and source of obstruction unrecorded.

evidence_for.relevance: Physical inspection verified internal obstruction in bypass path with handle in open position.
V-001 sustained internal damage consistent with obstructed bypass flow.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Procedural inadequacy in commissioning checklist relying solely on valve position rather than positive confirmation of bypass flow.

evidence_against.relevance: The existing written procedure was executed as specified per witness verification.

evidence_for.relevance: Commissioning checklist marked bypass opening complete without requiring verification of actual fluid passage.
Commissioning procedure was the existing safeguard intended to prevent startup deviation consequences.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Operator error during execution of FWKO start-up alignment procedures.

evidence_against.relevance: Post-event inspection confirmed the valve handle was placed in the indicated open position.
Time-stamped witness record documented operator moving the handle to open before start-up.
Commissioning checklist documents completion of the bypass opening step.

evidence_for.relevance: HAZOP deviation framing denotes error in FWKO start-up procedures.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Physical post-event inspection confirmed an internal obstruction in the bypass line despite the bypass valve handle being in the open position. A time-stamped witness verified the operator correctly placed the handle in the open position per the commissioning checklist. Internal damage to vessel V-001 was caused by the inability to establish flow through the obstructed bypass. The procedural failure to require positive flow verification contributed to the failure to detect the mechanical obstruction prior to start-up. Operator error is contradicted by physical and witness evidence.
uncertainty_notes: Specific composition, origin, and mechanism of the internal bypass obstruction are unrecorded.
Lack of pre-startup flow verification or pressure differential instrumentation data to establish the exact timing of blockage onset.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-STARTUP-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Start/Stop Procedures — Error in FWKO start-up procedures.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Possible internal damage to vessel V-001 and accessories.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: Commissioning procedure.
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] Post-event inspection found an internal obstruction in the bypass path despite the bypass-valve handle being in the indicated open position.
[E2] A time-stamped witness record documents the operator moving the bypass-valve handle to the indicated open position before start-up.
[E3] V-001 sustained internal damage after start-up. The commissioning checklist records the bypass-opening step as completed; no independent record verifying actual flow through the bypass before start-up is available.

# Task
Perform a neutral root-cause assessment.
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. Do not infer an operator action that is absent from the evidence record.
